requirements.description: Monthly stock returns, prices, shares outstanding, and exchange/share-code information for sample-period firms (1975-1993). Used for ME computation and BHAR/Ret12/Ret24/Ret36.
Point-in-time share code (shrcd) and exchange code (exchcd) to filter ordinary common shares (10/11) and NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ (1/2/3); also fiscal-year-end month from CRSP namelist.

Compustat annual fundamentals for B_t (book equity), B_{t-1}, B_{t-2}, NI_t (income before extraordinary items, Item 237), DIV_t (Item 21 = dvc), AT (total assets for the negative-earnings k fallback), and SALE (for 5-year sales growth).
Compustat company (static) for fiscal-year-end month (fyr), SIC code (sic), incorporation date (ipodate) for filtering fiscal year ends between June and December, and for FF industry mapping.
Link table joining Compustat gvkey to CRSP permno (permno/gvkey crosswalk), needed to compute ME = prc * shrout and to deliver analyst forecasts to firm-years.

I/B/E/S consensus EPS forecasts (meanest) by ticker/statistical-period/forecast-period for FY1 (fpi=1, fpedats ~ year t+1), FY2 (fpi=1, fpedats ~ year t+2), and the long-term growth forecast (Ltg) for May statistical periods of years 1976-1993.
I/B/E/S long-term (5-year) growth forecast (Ltg) used in Step 3 of the FROE construction. Typically carried in statsumu with measure='LTG' or similar; will require table search.
I/B/E/S identifier file linking ticker to cusip/oftic for join to Compustat gvkey via CRSP.

Fama-French 48-industry classification (FF 1997, Table 7) used to assign each firm a three-factor industry cost-of-equity. Not directly available in ClickHouse; must be constructed from Compustat SIC codes via a manual SIC->FF48 mapping table.

Three-factor industry cost-of-equity (FF 1997, Table 7) used to compute r_e for the EBO formula. Industry-specific risk premiums must be combined with a 6.46% risk-free rate. The premium table itself is not in ClickHouse; can be substituted with a published lookup table or with Compustat-derived industry indicators.

blocking_issues.reason: No FF 48-industry table in ClickHouse. Fama-French 48-industry classification (FF 1997) and industry cost-of-equity premiums are not pre-loaded.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Construct a hard-coded SIC-to-FF48 mapping (from the published FF 1997 Table 7 industry definitions) and apply it to comp_202601.company.sic for each firm-year. Cost-of-equity premiums will be loaded from a published lookup table (see assumptions.md).

blocking_issues.reason: Industry-specific cost-of-equity premiums (FF 1997 Table 7) are not in ClickHouse. The paper uses these as r_e in Eqs. 3.1-3.3. Without them V_h and V_f cannot be computed exactly; correlation with price (Table 2) and the per-firm V/P ratios (Tables 3, 4, 8, 9) are affected.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Use a hard-coded FF 1997 Table 7 lookup (48 industry codes x industry-specific risk premium). Combine with the 6.46% constant riskless rate. Document this as a CONVENTION-APPLIED default in assumptions.md. If a constant cost of equity (e.g., 12%) is substituted, all V_h/V_f values shift in lockstep but cross-sectional correlations and quintile ranks remain directionally correct.

blocking_issues.reason: I/B/E/S long-term growth (Ltg) is in statsumu_epsus with a 'measure' code that needs identification; the column is present but requires measure-value filtering (e.g., measure='LTG' or similar) which needs validation against the table.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Query ibes_202601.statsumu_epsus for distinct measure values during the sample window; use the long-term-growth measure. If unavailable, fall back to FROE_{t+1} = FROE_{t+2} per the paper's Appendix A Step 3 fallback (the paper explicitly documents this fallback).
